section_summary: This section records the Far Eastern Commission’s December 1946 policy on Japanese trade unions, its transmission as an occupation directive, and acknowledgment from Tokyo. It then follows the proposed 1947 visit of a World Federation of Trade Unions delegation, including American Federation of Labor objections and State Department correspondence. The section ends with the delegation’s preliminary report on labor conditions in Japan and Korea; its appended protest letter continues beyond page 67.

subfiles.title: Memorandum forwarding draft directive on Japanese trade unions
subfiles.about: Requests transmission of a draft occupation directive based on the Far Eastern Commission’s trade union policy.
subfiles.summary: Seeks Joint Chiefs of Staff transmission to MacArthur and acknowledgment of receipt.

subfiles.title: Draft directive regarding principles for Japanese trade unions
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Sets out sixteen principles for democratic Japanese trade unions.
subfiles.summary: The draft calls for legal protection, collective bargaining, limited strike restrictions, democratic elections, removal of repressive officials and organizations, and public financial accounts.

subfiles.title: Far Eastern Commission letter transmitting trade union policy
subfiles.about: Transmits the Commission’s unanimously approved policy for preparation of an occupation directive.
subfiles.summary: Johnson requests notice when the policy reaches Tokyo.

subfiles.title: Certification of Far Eastern Commission decision
subfiles.about: Certifies that the attached trade union decision matches the text adopted by the Commission.
subfiles.summary: Certifies the attached decision as a true copy.

subfiles.title: Principles for Japanese Trade Unions, FEC-045/5
subfiles.about: States the Commission’s sixteen policy principles governing Japanese trade unions.
subfiles.summary: The principles protect organization, speech, bargaining, political activity, and worker control of unions, while addressing strikes, purge rules, repressive agencies, and financial disclosure.

subfiles.title: Cover memorandum for directives 63, 64 and 65
subfiles.about: Forwards three Joint Chiefs of Staff directives for Commission and State Department files.
subfiles.summary: Identifies the recipients of copies of directives 63, 64 and 65.

subfiles.title: Directive 63: Principles for Japanese Trade Unions
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Transmits the Commission’s trade union principles as occupation guidance.
subfiles.summary: The final directive repeats the sixteen principles on union formation, negotiation, strikes, elections, political activity, removal of repressive structures, and financial accountability.

subfiles.title: Directive 64: Steel rolling industry reparations
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Makes surplus Japanese steel rolling capacity available as interim reparations.
subfiles.summary: Sets a retained production benchmark of 2,775,000 metric tons annually.

subfiles.title: Directive 65: Temporary retention of electric steel furnaces
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Permits temporary retention of specified electric steel furnace capacity during Japan’s coal shortage.
subfiles.summary: Allows temporary retention through June 1947, with review if extended.

subfiles.title: Memorandum filing directives with the Far Eastern Commission
subfiles.about: Sends certified copies of directives 63, 64 and 65 for Commission filing.
subfiles.summary: Lists the trade union and two reparations directives.

subfiles.title: Memorandum forwarding SCAP acknowledgment
subfiles.about: Forwards SCAP’s acknowledgment for transmission to the Far Eastern Commission.
subfiles.summary: Encloses the incoming acknowledgment message.

subfiles.title: SCAP acknowledgment of trade union directive
subfiles.to: War Department for Joint Chiefs of Staff
subfiles.about: Acknowledges receipt of the December 15 radio transmitting the directive.
subfiles.summary: Confirms receipt of radio W 87727.

subfiles.title: Duplicate memorandum forwarding SCAP acknowledgment
subfiles.about: Provides another copy of the memorandum forwarding the SCAP acknowledgment.
subfiles.summary: Copy accompanying the original memorandum.

subfiles.title: Copy of SCAP acknowledgment message
subfiles.to: War Department for Joint Chiefs of Staff
subfiles.about: Copies the acknowledgment of the December 15 directive radio.
subfiles.summary: Repeats the receipt acknowledgment on page 19.

subfiles.title: Memorandum notifying the Far Eastern Commission of acknowledgment
subfiles.about: Reports MacArthur’s acknowledgment of the trade union directive.
subfiles.summary: Requests circulation of the acknowledgment to Commission members.

subfiles.title: Compilation of Japanese Labor Union Statistics
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Transmits August 1946 Japanese union statistics and analysis compiled by SCAP.
subfiles.summary: Notes that monthly new-union figures are not cumulative totals.

subfiles.title: London airgram on British parliamentary questions about Japanese labor contacts
subfiles.about: Reports parliamentary discussion of renewed contact between Japanese and foreign labor organizations.
subfiles.summary: British officials favor eventual contact, subject to restored communications, and discuss foreign trade union visits and advisers.

subfiles.title: Moscow telegram on forthcoming WFTU visit
subfiles.about: Reports Soviet press notice of preparations for WFTU representatives to visit Japan.
subfiles.summary: Mentions Japanese union preparations and visiting youth delegates.

subfiles.title: Shanghai telegram concerning Chu Hsueh-fan’s entry to Japan
subfiles.about: Relays a request for Tokyo clearance for Chu Hsueh-fan’s proposed WFTU trip.
subfiles.summary: Shanghai says foreign visitors must seek permission through their own governments.

subfiles.title: Instruction to Shanghai to repeat Department telegram
subfiles.about: Instructs Shanghai to repeat an earlier Department telegram to Nanking and Hong Kong if needed.
subfiles.summary: Cross-references correspondence on WFTU travel clearance.

subfiles.title: Letter concerning Anglo-American petroleum agreement
subfiles.about: Requests a pause in action on a draft revision of the Anglo-American petroleum agreement.
subfiles.summary: An unrelated petroleum letter appears within the bundle.

subfiles.title: Department telegram on Chu Hsueh-fan clearance
subfiles.about: States that Tokyo clearance for WFTU representatives has not yet arrived.
subfiles.summary: The Department declines a special plea for Chu unless his government approves his visit.

subfiles.title: Nanking telegram on Chu Hsueh-fan request
subfiles.about: Supports Shanghai’s position against special American intervention for Chu’s visit.
subfiles.summary: The embassy prefers no action without Department instructions.

subfiles.title: French Embassy note requesting travel authorization for Saillant
subfiles.about: Requests authorization for Louis Saillant to visit Japan and Korea with the WFTU delegation.
subfiles.summary: The note anticipates the delegation’s arrival in Tokyo on March 20.

subfiles.title: Matthew Woll telegram protesting WFTU mission
subfiles.about: Protests permission for the WFTU delegation to visit Japanese unions.
subfiles.summary: Woll alleges Soviet influence over the WFTU, asks that its activity be restricted, and seeks publication of the AFL position in Japan.

subfiles.title: Charge-out slip for Woll telegram
subfiles.about: Records removal of the March 13 Woll telegram from the file.
subfiles.summary: Administrative charge-out record.

subfiles.title: Assistant Secretary note to Joe
subfiles.about: Comments on a proposed change to the last paragraph of a draft.
subfiles.summary: Handwritten editorial instruction; wording is partly illegible.

subfiles.title: Assistant Secretary note requesting review
subfiles.about: Asks colleagues to review a draft.
subfiles.summary: Brief handwritten review request.

subfiles.title: Assistant Secretary note concerning signature
subfiles.about: Raises a question about who should sign a draft.
subfiles.summary: Partly illegible handwritten signature query.

subfiles.title: Routing note attaching Woll telegram
subfiles.about: Attaches Woll’s telegram after a telephone discussion.
subfiles.summary: Brief note forwarding the protest telegram.

subfiles.title: Acheson reply to Matthew Woll
subfiles.about: Replies to Woll’s protest against the WFTU delegation’s visit.
subfiles.summary: Acheson cites Patterson’s explanation, current limits on Japanese WFTU affiliation, and earlier AFL visitors.

subfiles.title: Alternative draft reply to Matthew Woll
subfiles.about: Provides another version of the reply concerning the WFTU mission.
subfiles.summary: The draft emphasizes the mission’s limited size and duration.

subfiles.title: Memorandum explaining proposed reply to Woll
subfiles.about: Explains handling of Woll’s telegram and recommends a short State Department reply.
subfiles.summary: Notes War Department’s March 25 response and delayed internal receipt of Woll’s telegram.

subfiles.title: Memorandum reproducing Patterson’s reply to Woll
subfiles.about: Records the War Secretary’s explanation for authorizing the WFTU visit.
subfiles.summary: Patterson cites international considerations and argues that the short, supervised mission is unlikely to sway Japanese unions.

subfiles.title: Telegram to Shanghai on WFTU delegation travel
subfiles.about: Reports approval of the WFTU delegation trip and the status of individual travel permits.
subfiles.summary: Maintains that Chu needs approval from his own government.

subfiles.title: Charge-out slip for Woll reply
subfiles.about: Records removal of a file item relating to the Woll reply.
subfiles.summary: Administrative charge-out record.

subfiles.title: Moscow airgram reporting Soviet account of WFTU meeting
subfiles.about: Translates a Soviet press report on the WFTU delegation’s meeting with Japanese union leaders.
subfiles.summary: The report describes calls for Japanese union unification and eventual WFTU membership.

subfiles.title: Moscow telegram on Soviet article about Japanese elections
subfiles.about: Summarizes a Soviet article linking union and peasant movements to opposition to Yoshida’s government.
subfiles.summary: Requests that the report be repeated to Tokyo.

subfiles.title: Moscow telegram on Soviet article about Japanese trade unions
subfiles.about: Summarizes a Soviet article contrasting Japanese union groupings and welcoming WFTU contact.
subfiles.summary: Notes reported union membership and the creation of an all-Japan liaison council.

subfiles.title: Prague despatch transmitting WFTU report and resolution
subfiles.about: Transmits the WFTU delegation’s preliminary report and General Council resolution on Japan and Korea.
subfiles.summary: Lists enclosed report and resolution copies.

subfiles.title: Preliminary Report of the WFTU Delegation to Japan and Korea
subfiles.from: World Federation of Trade Unions delegation
subfiles.to: WFTU Executive Bureau and General Council
subfiles.about: Reports the delegation’s March–April 1947 inquiry into Japanese and Korean unions, working conditions and labor law.
subfiles.summary: The delegation describes its itinerary, access to officials and workplaces, and its recommendations for unified, democratic Japanese industrial unions. It urges improvements to food, housing, wages, equal pay, safety, social insurance and collective agreements. In South Korea it reports union repression and administrative failings, recommending legal protections and postponement or rejection of rival federations’ affiliation requests. In North Korea it recommends WFTU affiliation while calling for better working conditions and cooperation in reconstruction.

subfiles.title: Official WFTU protest letter to U.S. Military Government in Korea
subfiles.about: Begins an account of the delegation’s obstructed inspection of the Kyung Bong textile factory.
subfiles.summary: Names delegates and Korean companions and describes management blocking access to dormitories; the letter continues after page 67.
